slides.text: 2025 was a year of political noise, rollbacks, and broken promises in some corners of the world. But underneath it all, something remarkable was happening.

slides.caption: of global electricity came from zero-emissions sources in 2025. A new record — and it happened in April, not at year-end.

slides.text: Ireland closed its last coal plant in June — becoming the 6th European country to exit coal entirely. France ran its grid at 95% fossil-free for all of 2024.
For the first time ever, renewables generation surpassed coal globally. Not in a target document. In actual electricity produced — in October 2025.

slides.caption: cars sold worldwide in 2025 was electric. In Norway, that number was 99 in 100.

slides.text: Global deforestation is declining. Brazil's Amazon hit its lowest deforestation rate in a decade. China added 1 million hectares of wetlands since 2012.
slides.bold: lowest deforestation rate in a decade

slides.caption: of our oceans gained new protection when the High Seas Treaty entered into force in September 2025.

slides.text: China's CO2 emissions were flat or falling for 18 consecutive months. Its clean energy sector grew to 10% of GDP — larger than its entire property sector.
slides.bold: flat or falling for 18 consecutive months

slides.caption: of all new US energy jobs in 2024 came from clean energy — growing 3× faster than the rest of the workforce.

slides.text: None of this means the problem is solved. But the energy transition is no longer a plan. It is happening — faster than almost anyone predicted.
